* Literature links CO2 emissions, economic growth
  - Kaya identity decomposes CO2: population, GDP, energy intensity, carbon intensity
  - EKC evidence remains mixed: income, trade, energy-mix dependent
  - Early studies emphasize energy use, industrial structure, policy constraints
* Decoupling separates growth, emissions
  - Green innovation, renewable energy, carbon tax, cap-and-trade reduce emissions
  - Absolute, relative decoupling requires efficiency, structural transformation
  - Empirical tests report decoupling, clean-energy adoption, efficiency gains
* Energy mix shapes emissions
  - Fossil-fuel dominance raises carbon intensity
  - Solar, wind, nuclear, hydro lower emissions, scaling required
  - Energy security, affordability, grid reliability constrain transition
* Trade, openness, specialization affect emissions
  - Exporting polluting sectors raises national CO2; importing clean goods lowers domestic CO2
  - Environmental standards, technology transfer, supply-chain design matter
* Policy instruments target low-carbon growth
  - Carbon pricing, emissions trading, subsidies, efficiency standards curb CO2
  - NDCs, green finance, technology transfer accelerate mitigation
  - Stringent, stable, predictable regulations attract clean investment
* Research gaps require methods, data improvements
  - Panel, threshold, spatial econometrics, machine learning improve causality
  - Heterogeneity: regions, sectors, income levels, energy transitions
  - Long-run, sectoral, sub-national datasets strengthen evidence
